title: Chapter 21 — Panel-Ready & The Integration Craft
intro: The integrated kitchen as a system — millwork coordination and fit disciplines.

sections.title: The Fully Integrated Kitchen
sections.content:
A fully integrated kitchen means every appliance disappears behind custom cabinetry. The dishwasher, refrigerator, freezer — all panel-ready. The range or cooktop is the only visible appliance, and even that can be minimized with a flush-mount induction cooktop.

This is the highest-end kitchen design and it requires the most coordination. Every panel dimension, every hinge specification, every handle placement must be communicated between the appliance retailer, the cabinet maker, and the installer.

Your role in this conversation is not just selling appliances — it is being the technical bridge between the design vision and the installation reality.

sections.title: Coordination Disciplines
sections.content:
For every panel-ready unit, verify the panel spec sheet from the manufacturer. It specifies maximum panel weight, thickness, hinge type, and handle position. Give this to the cabinetmaker before they start building.

Document every measurement on the quote. The cutout dimensions for columns. The depth clearance behind panel-ready dishwashers. The ventilation space above built-in refrigeration.

Schedule a pre-delivery review with the installer. Walk through every unit, every panel, every connection point. One missed spec means a delayed installation and an unhappy customer who has already paid for custom cabinetry.

This level of coordination is what separates the $50,000 kitchen sale from the $5,000 kitchen sale. It is also what earns you the designer referral for the next project.

sections.title: Common Integration Mistakes
sections.content:
Panel ordered wrong thickness — does not fit the appliance frame. Handle holes drilled in the wrong position — panel has to be remade. Ventilation clearance not accounted for — built-in fridge overheats. Counter depth not verified — appliance protrudes past cabinet face.

Every one of these mistakes is preventable with the spec sheet and a tape measure. Every one costs hours of rework and thousands in remaking custom panels.

The rep who gets integration right every time becomes the designer's go-to. The one who gets it wrong once may never get a second chance. In luxury, you are only as good as your last installation.
